name: Crab Nebula
distance_method: VLBI radio trigonometric parallax of the Crab pulsar (0.53 +/- 0.06 mas -> 1.90 +0.22/-0.18 kpc)
source: Lin, van Kerkwijk, Kirsten, Pen & Deller 2023, ApJ (arXiv:2306.01617)
notes: Paper states consistency with Gaia DR3. Classic value 2.0 +/- 0.5 kpc (Trimble 1973). Coordinates from SIMBAD (M 1).

name: Lagoon Nebula
distance_method: Gaia DR2 parallax of ionizing/embedded cluster NGC 6530 (0.75 +/- 0.04 mas, 669 stars)
source: Kuhn, Hillenbrand, Sills, Feigelson & Getman 2019, ApJ 870, 32 (Gaia DR2 cluster parallaxes, Table 1)
notes: Distance is to NGC 6530, the young cluster embedded in the Lagoon. Coordinates from SIMBAD (M 8).

name: Eagle Nebula
distance_method: Gaia DR2 parallax of ionizing cluster NGC 6611 (0.57 +/- 0.04 mas, 356 stars)
source: Kuhn, Hillenbrand, Sills, Feigelson & Getman 2019, ApJ 870, 32 (Gaia DR2 cluster parallaxes, Table 1)
notes: Coordinates from SIMBAD (M 16, which SIMBAD treats as the cluster NGC 6611). SIMBAD also lists Cantat-Gaudin et al. 2020 cluster parallax 0.566 +/- 0.006 mas, consistent.

name: Omega Nebula (Swan Nebula)
distance_method: Gaia DR2 parallax of ionizing cluster NGC 6618 (0.60 +/- 0.04 mas, 82 stars)
source: Kuhn, Hillenbrand, Sills, Feigelson & Getman 2019, ApJ 870, 32 (Gaia DR2 cluster parallaxes, Table 1)

name: Trifid Nebula
type: emission nebula / H II region (with reflection nebula component)
distance_method: Gaia DR2 parallax of the ionizing cluster (0.79 +/- 0.05 mas, 116 stars)
source: Kuhn, Hillenbrand, Sills, Feigelson & Getman 2019, ApJ 870, 32 (Gaia DR2 cluster parallaxes, Table 1)
notes: Kuhn et al. note this is ~2x nearer than the older 2700 pc estimate (Cambresy et al. 2011). Coordinates from SIMBAD (M 20).

name: Small Sagittarius Star Cloud
notes: No single distance is meaningful: M24 is a window through dust onto Milky Way stars spread over a long line of sight (roughly 10,000 ly deep, mostly in the Sagittarius-Carina arm and beyond). distance_ly left null deliberately. Coordinates from SIMBAD (M 24, approximate centre).

name: Dumbbell Nebula
distance_method: Gaia EDR3 trigonometric parallax of central star (2.570 +/- 0.037 mas), simple inversion
source: Gaia EDR3 parallax of central star (Gaia Collaboration 2020, VizieR I/350), as listed in SIMBAD
notes: Range is +/-1 sigma in parallax; no zero-point correction applied (affects ~1%). Coordinates are the central star position from SIMBAD.

name: Winnecke 4
distance_method: not applicable (optical double); component parallaxes from Gaia EDR3
source: Gaia EDR3 parallaxes via SIMBAD (VizieR I/350): HD 238107 = 3.219 +/- 0.012 mas; HD 238108 = 6.933 +/- 0.016 mas
notes: The two stars are unrelated line-of-sight neighbours: HD 238107 ~ 1013 ly (311 pc), HD 238108 ~ 470 ly (144 pc). A single distance for 'M40' is not meaningful, so distance_ly is null; per-star values given here. Coordinates are SIMBAD's nominal M 40 position.

name: Orion Nebula
distance_method: Gaia DR2 parallax of the Orion Nebula Cluster (2.48 +/- 0.04 mas, 378 stars)
source: Kuhn, Hillenbrand, Sills, Feigelson & Getman 2019, ApJ 870, 32 (Gaia DR2 cluster parallaxes, Table 1)
notes: Other values: 414 +/- 7 pc (Menten et al. 2007, VLBA), 388 +/- 5 pc (Kounkel et al. 2017, VLBA), 386 +/- 3 pc (Kounkel et al. 2018, Gaia DR2). Spread across methods (~1260-1350 ly) exceeds the quoted error. Coordinates from SIMBAD (M 42).

name: De Mairan's Nebula
distance_method: Adopted Orion Nebula Cluster Gaia DR2 distance (M43 is part of the same Orion A complex, ionized by NU Ori)
source: Kuhn, Hillenbrand, Sills, Feigelson & Getman 2019, ApJ 870, 32 (Gaia DR2 cluster parallaxes, Table 1)
notes: No independent distance to M43/NU Ori was looked up; value is the ONC distance, assumed to apply because M43 is separated from M42 only by a dust lane. Coordinates from SIMBAD (M 43).

name: Ring Nebula
distance_method: Gaia EDR3 trigonometric parallax of central star (1.270 +/- 0.044 mas), simple inversion
source: Gaia EDR3 parallax of central star (Gaia Collaboration 2020, VizieR I/350), as listed in SIMBAD
notes: Range is +/-1 sigma in parallax; no zero-point correction applied. Coordinates are the central star position from SIMBAD.

name: NGC 6994 (asterism)
source: Odenkirchen & Soubiran 2002, A&A 383, 163: 'NGC 6994 - clearly not a physical stellar ensemble'
notes: Spectroscopy and proper motions show the ~4-6 bright stars have different kinematics and lie at different distances: a chance alignment of unrelated Milky Way field stars. No single distance is meaningful, so distance_ly is null. SIMBAD otype is 'err' (non-existent cluster). Coordinates from SIMBAD (NGC 6994).

name: Little Dumbbell Nebula
distance_method: Statistical planetary-nebula distance (not a direct measurement)
source: Phillips 2005, MNRAS 357, 619, 'The distances of highly evolved planetary nebulae' (as cited by Wikipedia; value not verified in the paper itself)
notes: Distance ~780 pc (~2,500 ly) is very uncertain; no formal error bar sourced, so low/high are null. Gaia EDR3 central-star parallax 0.29 +/- 0.20 mas (SIMBAD) is too imprecise (1.5 sigma) to give a useful distance. Coordinates are central star position from SIMBAD.

name: NGC 2068
distance_method: Gaia DR2 parallaxes of APOGEE-2 young stellar members of the NGC 2068 group (417 +/- 5 pc)
source: Kounkel et al. 2018, AJ 156, 84, 'The APOGEE-2 Survey of the Orion Star Forming Complex II: Six-dimensional structure'
notes: Part of the Orion B molecular cloud (Orion B average 407 +/- 4 pc in same paper). Coordinates from SIMBAD (M 78).

name: Owl Nebula
distance_method: Gaia EDR3 trigonometric parallax of central star (1.235 +/- 0.046 mas), simple inversion
source: Gaia EDR3 parallax of central star (Gaia Collaboration 2020, VizieR I/350), as listed in SIMBAD
notes: Range is +/-1 sigma in parallax; no zero-point correction applied. Coordinates are the central star position from SIMBAD.

name: NGC 5866 (Spindle Galaxy) - disputed identification
distance_method: not researched (out of scope for this nebula batch)
source: Wikipedia 'Messier 102' (Mechain's 1783 letter to J. Bernoulli retracting M102 as a duplicate of M101); SIMBAD resolves 'M 102' to NGC 5866
notes: Identification disputed: Mechain later called M102 an accidental duplicate of M101, but Messier's handwritten notes and the catalogue description best match NGC 5866, which SIMBAD and NASA adopt. It is an external galaxy, not a nebula, so milky_way=false. Distance left null (not looked up). Coordinates from SIMBAD (NGC 5866).
